chapter_title: Concept of Mole and Chemical Calculation

sections.content_markdown:
Now, we'll divide the quotients by the small quotient above:

$$C = \frac{7.69}{7.69} = 1$$

$$H = \frac{7.69}{7.69} = 1$$

So, the empirical formula of the compound: $\text{C}_1\text{H}_1 = \text{CH}$

Since the empirical formula is $\text{CH}$, the molecular formula will be $(\text{CH})_n = \text{C}_n\text{H}_n$

The mass of empirical formula of the compound stands $= 12 \times 1 + 1 \times 1 = 13$ and its molecular mass $= 78$

Therefore $n = \frac{\text{molecular mass of compound}}{\text{mass of empirical formula}} = \frac{78}{13} = 6$

Thus, the molecular formula of the compound is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$

sections.section_title: Determining Molecular Formula from Empirical Formula
sections.content_markdown:
The molecular formula of a compound can be the base to determine its empirical formula. Suppose, we need to find the empirical formula of glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$).

A glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) molecule consists of $06$ $\text{C}$ atoms, $12$ $\text{H}$ atoms and $06$ $\text{O}$ atoms.

The ratio of atoms $\text{C} : \text{H} : \text{O} = 6 : 12 : 6 = 1 : 2 : 1$

Therefore, the empirical formula of glucose is $\text{C}_1\text{H}_2\text{O}_1 = \text{CH}_2\text{O}$

Sometimes, the empirical formula and molecular formula are similar. For example, the molecular formula of water is $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, its empirical formula is $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ too. Both the formulas for sulfuric acid is $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

Usually, the compounds, all the atoms of which can be divided by a certain number, have different molecular and empirical formulas. The molecular formula of benzene is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$. Since the number of atoms here are divisible by $6$, therefore, its empirical formula will be $\text{C}_1\text{H}_1 = \text{CH}$. Similarly, the molecular formula of ethene is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$. Therefore, its empirical formula is $\text{C}_1\text{H}_2 = \text{CH}_2$.
